Selected projects / Evidence first

Projects by Nolan Kido

Nolan Kido / Public portfolio

What has Nolan Kido built and published?

I make practical AI tools, test software against specific tasks, and work on creative projects involving writing and tournament poker. AI Works, Human Decides connects the work: give a tool a defined job, inspect what happened, and keep consequential choices with people.

This is a selected public portfolio, not a claim that every prototype has launched or that a demonstration proves business results. The links distinguish tools you can try now, recorded application examples, and published work that other people can independently identify.

Try free toolsInspect applicationsReview the evidenceSee creative and research work

Use / No account required

Three tools you can use directly.

These are browser-based utilities. They are useful for working through a decision, but they do not run a remote AI model or establish that the result is correct.

Practical AI / Task preparation

AI Task Brief Builder

Use it for: turning an unclear request into a task with permitted inputs, a finish line, acceptance checks, and a person responsible for approval.

What it demonstrates: a structured brief assembled locally from your own entries. It does not call an AI model or measure time saved. Inspect the method.

Practical AI / Full-workflow cost

AI Workflow Time Calculator

Use it for: comparing setup, drafting, checking, corrections, and maintenance instead of counting only the first AI response.

What it demonstrates: transparent arithmetic using figures you enter. Its sample scenarios are fictional, not a measured productivity study.

Poker / Review away from play

Poker Study Calculators

Use it for: checking pot-odds and other basic poker quantities with the assumptions on the page.

What it demonstrates: calculations for study, not a complete poker strategy, an ICM solver, or real-time play assistance.

Software / Archived examples

Three applications with inspectable cases.

Each project record explains the problem, shows a bounded example, and states what remains unverified. An archived demonstration is not a guarantee of a production service.

Local AI / Customer communication

Review Reply Writer

A local-model workflow for drafting customer-review responses without authorizing promises or sending a response automatically. Its worked double-charge review is fictional.

Inspect: the example and approval boundary, then the separate audit of archived replies. Neither record establishes a production error rate or client outcomes.

Writing / Source-linked continuity

Preflight

A manuscript-checking project that compares passages and proposes possible continuity problems. An archived Sherlock Holmes example includes both useful flags and mistakes.

Inspect: the passages beside the report. A suggestion is not an editorial verdict, and the archived test is not a general accuracy claim.

Everyday planning / Simulation

Dinner on Time

A cooking-planner demonstration that changes upcoming steps when an oven becomes unavailable while preserving recorded progress.

Inspect: the recorded simulation. The scenario is a demonstration, not evidence that it was used in a real household or that every possible cooking change is safe.

Evidence / Corrections / Limits

What can a reader actually verify?

Three different records show why I separate a useful output from a verified outcome:

  1. Measured software behavior: the local-model test record preserves timings, errors, and environment details from an Ubuntu CPU runner. It does not provide a measured speed claim for my Windows laptop or a customer deployment.
  2. A public correction: checking an AI-assisted website change follows a real HTML defect through separate release checks. Passing one set of tests did not establish that the page was valid.
  3. A human review boundary: a poker hand record becomes proposed captions, with source limits and reproducible chip arithmetic. The example does not certify the current video cut or supply missing solver inputs.

For the practical method behind these projects, read AI Works, Human Decides. If you are checking a particular claim, start with the linked record, its date, its original inputs, and what the published test did not evaluate.

Work beyond software

Poker stories, illustration, and scholarship.

  • NolanPoker and tournament records: first-person video links, written companions for selected episodes, and independently reported event results where available. A gross cash is not a profit figure, and narration is not third-party verification of every hand.
  • Illustrated poker explanations: AI-assisted comics with readable text and rules notes. Fictional scenes are presented as teaching material, not tournament footage.
  • Published accounting research: my coauthored 2012 Journal of Accounting Research paper on elections and governmental accounting choices. That publication supports research authorship, not a current appointment or an AI-model result.

I also enjoy building games, wine tasting, food, and travel. Those interests matter, but an unfinished game or an unpublished note is not listed here as a finished public release. As inspectable work becomes available, it can earn its own project record rather than a speculative launch claim.
